form.label: MITRE ATT&CK
form.description: Which adversary techniques the fleet's open vulnerabilities could enable.

div.b: This page shows exposure, not attack evidence.
div.span: CVE → CWE → CAPEC → ATT&CK technique is a published MITRE mapping: many-to-many and lossy. It says this weakness class is the kind of thing that enables that technique, not that anyone used it or that the CVE is exploitable here. A CVE with no CWE, or an unmapped CWE, never appears - absence is not safety. For real-world exploitation rather than classification, see KEV and EPSS on Findings.

panel.title: ATT&CK matrix - where open findings sit in an attack

search.query: | `riskability_attack_matrix_for($host_tok|s$, $conf_tok|s$)` | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY tactic_name, tactic_order, technique_name | eventstats max(cves) AS peak BY technique_name | sort 50000 - peak | head 120 | sort 50000 tactic_order | fields tactic_name, technique_name, cves

viz.option: No tactic data. The ATT&CK tactic mapping is missing from the bundle, not the exposure - rebuild with --mitre and import.

div.b: An empty matrix means the tactic mapping is missing.
div.span: The grid needs MITRE's technique-to-tactic mapping, carried only by bundles a recent feed builder built with --mitre: rebuild and import. Without tactics the technique list below is still correct, just not placeable in an attack sequence. Cells count distinct CVEs; a technique appears under every tactic MITRE assigns it, so a row counts the same CVEs more than once.

panel.title: Techniques enabled by open findings, most exposed first

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface_for($host_tok|s$, $conf_tok|s$)` | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves, dc(hostname) AS hosts, dc(package) AS packages, values(cwe) AS weaknesses, max(epss) AS peak_epss BY technique, technique_name | eval peak_epss = round(peak_epss, 4) | sort 50000 - cves | rename technique AS "Technique", technique_name AS "Name", cves AS "CVEs", hosts AS "Hosts", packages AS "Packages", weaknesses AS "Via CWE", peak_epss AS "Peak EPSS"

viz.option: No open finding maps to a technique. Most CVEs carry no CWE: usually a mapping gap, not an absence of exposure.

panel.title: Weakness classes present in the fleet (CWE)

search.query: | `riskability_finding_cwes_for($host_tok|s$, "*")` | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY cwe | sort 50000 - cves | head 40

viz.option: No open finding carries a CWE. Most CVEs have no recorded weakness class: a mapping gap, not an absence of risk. See the coverage panel.

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings_for($host_tok|s$)` | lookup riskability_advisory_lookup cve_id OUTPUT cwes | eval mapped = case(isnull(cwes) OR cwes=="", "no CWE recorded for this CVE", 1=1, "has a CWE") | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY mapped | eventstats sum(cves) AS total | eval share = round(cves*100/total, 1)."%" | fields mapped, cves, share | rename mapped AS "Mapping status", cves AS "CVEs", share AS "Share"

panel.title: Which weaknesses lead to which techniques - $tech_label$

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface_for($host_tok|s$, $conf_tok|s$)` | search $tech_filter$ $cwe_filter$ | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY cwe, technique_name | sort 50000 - cves | head 25

viz.option: No open finding has a CWE that MITRE links to a technique.

div.span: One weakness can enable several techniques, so a CVE is drawn once per technique it reaches. Each ribbon is correct alone (that many distinct CVEs link that CWE to that technique), but totals double-count. Read concentration, not totals. Top 25 links only.

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface_for($host_tok|s$, $conf_tok|s$)` | search $tech_filter$ $cwe_filter$ | stats min(epss) AS lo, perc25(epss) AS q1, median(epss) AS med, perc75(epss) AS q3, max(epss) AS hi, dc(cve_id) AS cves BY technique_name | where cves >= 3 | sort 50000 - cves | head 15 | fields technique_name, lo, q1, med, q3, hi

viz.option: Not enough scored CVEs per technique to plot a distribution. EPSS comes from the feed; without it in the bundle there is nothing to plot.

div.b: Boxes show the EPSS spread per technique, not its peak.
div.span: The table above reports each technique's highest EPSS, which one CVE can dominate; a box separates many likely-exploited CVEs from a single outlier. Techniques with fewer than three scored CVEs are omitted.
Click a technique, matrix cell, CWE tile, Sankey ribbon or box below to narrow this page to it.
Page narrowed. The panels below show only what matches; the matrix and technique list stay whole so you can pick something else.

These findings are real vulnerabilities. The technique is what MITRE says this weakness class could enable, not something anyone observed, and it is two steps removed from the CVE: the advisory names a weakness class, and that class maps to techniques. A technique can therefore read oddly for a particular CVE. Read the "What it is" column first and treat the technique as the category, not the finding. Read the technique on attack.mitre.org (needs internet).

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface_detail_for($host_tok|s$, $conf_tok|s$)` | search $tech_filter$ $cwe_filter$ | eval root = if(scope_id!="", scope_id, "host") | eval installed_version = last_version | table cve_id, title, severity, epss, package, installed_version, fixed_version, hostname, root, technique, technique_name, cwe, via_capec | sort 50000 technique, - epss | rename cve_id AS "CVE", title AS "What it is", severity AS "Severity", epss AS "EPSS", package AS "Package", installed_version AS "Installed", fixed_version AS "Fixed in", hostname AS "Host", root AS "Root", technique AS "Technique", technique_name AS "Technique name", cwe AS "CWE", via_capec AS "Via CAPEC"

viz.option: No findings map to a technique at this confidence filter.
